subject: hydra
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: five-headed hydra.
Style: God of War.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module to build a five-headed hydra in a dark, gritty God of War aesthetic—bulky quadruped body, heavy tail, scarred armored plating, muted colors with red accents and glowing embers, using only well-understood SDK APIs since I can't test the code.

Sizing it up: body roughly 4m long with shoulders around 2.2m, necks stretching up to 5-6m, five heads each with hinged jaws, horns, and glowing eyes. For style I'm layering in charred skin, scars, bone armor, bronze bands, broken spears embedded in its back, a chained iron cuff on one neck, and rune marks glowing red with ember light in the mouths.

Now I'm working out the skeleton structure—placing hip joints, body dimensions, leg positions, and where the necks branch off the chest and shoulders, since the hydra needs to face forward along one axis with legs supporting the bulk via IK.

Writing spine and tail chains...

I'll leave the spine joint count at the default of 3, using names spine1-3. For the tail, I'm building a 5-point catmull curve from the hips down to a tapered tip, parented to hips as a "tail" chain with joints tail1-5 and decreasing radii from 0.62 down to 0.08.

Now I'm thinking about adding five separate neck chains sprouting from the chest area, spread across the x-axis, each one defined as its own chain parented to spine3 rather than relying on an automatic sprout function.

Each neck follows a five-point curve rising up then sweeping forward-down in a swan-like arc, so the terminal tangent naturally aims the head forward and slightly downward.

For the skeleton, I'm planning joint chains with named segments for necks, head, jaw, spine, tail, and legs, keeping total joint count manageable around seventy. For a five-point chain I need five matching names so the tip joint gets included rather than stopping one short.

Now I'm working out how the head joint attaches to the neck's tip, pulling the direction from the path's end tangent and tilting it slightly downward for a natural pose.

I realize numeric local coordinates (right, forward, up) will follow head tilt better than world-aligned ones, so I'll define a helper using that convention, with side symmetry handled by a sign flag for left/right.

I'm sketching a buildHead function that places skull, jaw, and facial parts as primitive shapes attached to bones, using local coordinate offsets scaled by a size factor, while being careful about how orientation defaults work when no explicit rotation is given.

Defining more head parts...

Still figuring out jaw geometry...

Still working out teeth placement...

For eyes I'm thinking a small glowing ember-orange sphere near the brow, paired with a dark slit pupil for an angry look, possibly textured with a radial gradient and black slit rendered via SVG wrapped onto the sphere.

I'll normalize the direction vector manually with helper vector math, and bump the glow strength for eyes to 1.6. For the brow ridge I'm placing an angled bone-colored rod over the eye socket, and for horns I'm planning two main swept-back bezier horns from the skull plus smaller cheek spikes, all in a banded bone color.

For the neck frill, I'm figuring out how dorsal spines should orient along the sweep -- since the neck curves vertically like an S, the "outward" normal shifts direction, so spikes point backward on vertical stretches and upward on horizontal ones to stay consistent with the tube's surface.

Now I'm setting up the paint scheme: dark charcoal-green scales on the back with a paler ash/ochre countershade for the belly, defining the actual color values for each.

Adding scar generation logic...

Finishing the hide paint logic to add ember cracks with a cell-based threshold, falling back to the base countershade otherwise. I need to pull in noise, cells, paint, mix, smoothstep, and resolve from the SDK's single export module, and confirm paints bake efficiently per texel. Now I'm thinking about armor details — segmented bone plates running along the spine and a shoulder pauldron, inspired by God of War's Norse aesthetic.

I'm also adding Kratos-style iron chains and shackles around the necks, broken spears lodged in the hydra's back, and a bronze cuff, plus glowing ember rune decals on the shoulder plates. For the five heads I'm varying their scale and giving each personality: a broken horn on one, a crowned flame-breathing centerpiece, and a scarred blind-eyed head with an iron muzzle. I'm adding a glowing ember-colored throat interior inside each mouth and posing the jaw slightly open by rotating it on its hinge.

Working out the jaw rotation axis so the lower jaw tips down correctly given the head's yaw, and planning to apply this pose only after all jaw parts and surface frames are attached, since earlier geometry is stored relative to the unposed frame.

Now I'm designing a forked tongue for a couple of the heads, sweeping from inside the jaw outward with a reddish color, then moving on to leg placement — hips and shoulders positioned along a spine running from the lower back up to the chest, with hind legs attached at the hip points.

Working out leg segment lengths and bend directions...

With 4 points and 3 spans, I'll assign 4 names: hipHL, kneeHL, ankleHL, footHL as the tip, aiming the tip along the end tangent. For chains of three or more segments, I'm making the last segment parallel to the root direction for natural bending.

I'm working out the hind leg bends with knee forward and hock back, and front leg positioning with elbow back and wrist forward, checking that total reach exceeds the vertical distance so the legs can fold properly. For leg thickness I'm tapering radii along each chain from thigh to shin to ankle.

Now I'm placing the paw as a flattened sphere scaled to form a wide clawed foot, positioning it just above floor level relative to the foot joint's tip frame.

Adding toe claws and shin armor...

Still working out the ring placement...

Still defining leg radius function...

For dorsal plates, I'm placing flattened cone shapes along the spine sweep, using scale tricks to make them wide and spiky, tapering their size along the row.

I also want a secondary scatter of smaller bone knobs across the flanks using a surface scatter filtered to upward-facing normals, plus bone pauldrons as half-spheres over the shoulders and hips, and a few broken spears jutting from the torso surface with wooden shafts and bronze heads.

Breaking spears into shaft stubs with splintered spike tips instead. Now I'm thinking about adding an iron chain hanging from one neck's shackle collar, built from a repeated torus-link pattern along a hanging path down to the ground.

I'll pass an explicit bone override for the chain pieces so they rigidly follow the neck joint rather than relying on path-derived bone inference. For torus orientation, I need to figure out the axis/dir combination so the ring plane contains the tangent rather than being perpendicular to it, since the default torus axis sits along local Z.

For elongating the links, scaling the torus geometry itself before instancing (rather than scaling in the frame) seems cleaner since the roll direction from the aim orientation is somewhat arbitrary.

I'll settle the frame orientation that way and move on to chain geometry: computing link spacing from a path running from the neck shackle down to the ground, with torus dimensions set so roughly 50 links cover the ~4.5m length, which keeps the part count manageable. I'm also double-checking the neck position relative to the body before placing the chain's starting point.

Now I'm planning distinct neck decorations: an iron shackle with chain on one neck, a spiked bone ring on another, a glowing gold-bronze collar on the central boss, and a wrapped rope-like texture on another, giving each of the five necks a visually unique treatment.

Since I don't know if the rasterizer supports runic fonts, I'm drawing the Elder Futhark-style runes as simple stroked paths instead, building an orange-red glowing rune strip texture to decal onto a shoulder plate or collar.

I'm planning to apply these rune decals as "brand" sigils on the flanks and haunches using the decal function with a texture parameter, making sure the material is a standard MeshStandardMaterial so the glow effect works correctly. Now I'm sketching the eye texture as an SVG with a radial orange-yellow gradient and a black vertical slit pupil against a dark rim.

I'm counting up the texture assets I'll need — something like 5-12 total: normal eye, blind eye, a rune sigil, a rune collar strip, and maybe a flame card glowing in the center head's mouth for an ember effect, plus possibly bone-pale bristle mane tufts along the neck.

For those bristle ridges, I'm planning to scatter dark spiky cards along the spine and each neck sweep, filtering by height so they sit on the upper curve, with modest counts per neck (around 14 each across 5 necks, one mesh per texture for efficiency) to give that gritty God of War-style silhouette. Now I'm settling on bone color palettes — aged ivory and a darker shade for contrast.

For metals, I'm pulling iron and bronze presets from the clockwork kit, applying verdigris and tarnish to bronze for collar pieces and plain iron for chains, plus the glow kit for the embers at the eyes, mouth interior, and spine cracks — staying flat-shaded since this isn't a toon style. I'm keeping the color count well under the 64-flat-color limit, skipping a ground plane since it's not needed, and now working out torso proportions for the underbelly and seat height.

Now I'm laying out the actual joint coordinates for the hips and spine chain, then sweeping the torso body across that spine with varying radii — narrower at the hips, widening through the mid-back and chest, with the cross-section growing rounder toward the top.

Still writing interpolation helper...

With jaw joint at z=-0.095, the box top lands at -0.05, giving a slight overlap with the upper jaw bottom at -0.075, which actually works since the teeth can slip into that overlap and the jaw can still open on a 15° pose rotation. For the cheek frills, instead of extruded plates I'll use swept-back bone spikes on each side of the head, computing their direction and length in the head's local coordinate space so they angle backward from the cheek. For horn coloring, I'm deciding between a gradient function versus discrete color bands since horns typically look pale near the tip and darker at the base -- bands seem cleaner since they split the tube's color at an exact point rather than blending.

Then I'm planning the smaller secondary horns, including a snout spike with its own position and direction, plus brow ridges using rod shapes, eye placement, small dark nostril spheres, and a facial scar rendered as a thin pale sweep across the skull surface.

Working out the scar geometry now, trying a flattened box versus a rod connecting two points on the cranium's ellipsoid surface, picking an angle parameter to place it convincingly along the curve of the skull.
